title: How to Fight Anxiety With Scripture
excerpt: You cannot argue yourself out of anxiety. But you can preach to yourself, and the question is only which voice gets the last word, your fear or the word of God.
body:
Anxiety is a liar that speaks in your own voice, which is what makes it so hard to fight. It does not feel like an outside attack. It feels like the truth, like the most honest assessment of how bad things really are. And so we cannot simply decide to stop being anxious, any more than we can decide to stop hearing a voice that sounds exactly like our own thoughts.

But we are not without help. The Scriptures are full of anxious people, David hiding in caves, Elijah wanting to die, the disciples certain the boat would sink, and they are full of God's response to fear, which is not contempt but a steady, repeated word. "Do not be afraid" appears in the Bible more than any other command. God knew what kind of creatures he was speaking to. He gave us his word to fight the lie with the truth.

## Understand what you are actually doing

Fighting anxiety with Scripture is not magic, and it is not denial. You are not pretending the hard thing is not hard. You are putting a truer word over the false one. Anxiety preaches a sermon all day long, that you are alone, that it depends on you, that the worst will happen and you will not survive it. The fight is to preach a better sermon back, in God's words, until his voice is louder than the fear's.

This is a fight, and it is daily, and you will not win it once and for all. The goal is not to stop the anxious thought from arriving. The goal is to have something true to answer it with when it does.

## Choose a few passages and learn them by heart

Anxiety does not wait for you to find your Bible. It shows up at three in the morning, in the car, in the middle of a meeting, when you have nothing in front of you but the fear. So you have to carry the word inside you, where the fear lives. Choose a small number of passages and learn them by heart so they are available when you need them.

Good places to start. Philippians 4:6-7, do not be anxious, but in everything by prayer bring it to God, and his peace will guard you. Matthew 6:25-34, look at the birds, your Father feeds them, are you not worth more. Psalm 23, the shepherd who is with you in the valley. Isaiah 41:10, fear not, I am with you, I will uphold you. Pick two or three. Learn them cold.

## Pray the passage, do not just recite it

When the anxiety hits, do not merely repeat the verse like a charm. Pray it. Take Philippians 4 and actually do what it says, name the specific thing you are afraid of, bring it to God in detail, and ask for the peace it promises. Take Psalm 23 and pray it slowly, line by line, applying each phrase to the valley you are actually in. The word is not a spell. It is a door into prayer, and prayer is where the anxiety meets the God who is bigger than it.

## Replace the lie out loud

Anxiety is verbal. It talks. So talk back, out loud if you can. When the fear says "you are alone in this," answer it out loud with "I am not alone, God is with me, he said so." When it says "you will not be able to handle this," answer "I do not have to handle it alone, and his grace is enough." Saying it aloud matters, because it puts a second voice in the room, and the anxious voice loses some of its monopoly the moment another voice answers it.

## Do it before the crisis, not just during

The time to build this habit is not at the peak of a panic, when you can barely think. It is in the calm hours, every day, when you can sit with the passages and let them sink in. A soldier does not learn to load his weapon during the battle. He learns it in the quiet, by repetition, so that in the chaos his hands already know what to do. Soak in the verses daily, and they will be there waiting on the night you need them.

## Know when anxiety needs more than Scripture

This is important, and I will not soften it. Sometimes anxiety is not only a spiritual battle but a medical one. Panic attacks, anxiety that will not lift for weeks, anxiety that keeps you from sleeping or working or leaving the house, anxiety with physical symptoms you cannot control, these may be signs of a clinical condition that needs a doctor or a counselor. Seeing one is not a failure of faith. God heals through medicine and through trained people just as truly as through prayer. If your anxiety is that heavy, please get help. Fighting with Scripture and getting professional care are not rivals. Do both.

## This week

Choose one passage, Philippians 4:6-7 is a good start, and write it on a card. Carry the card. Read it every morning until you know it without looking. Then, the next time anxiety rises, pull the verse up from memory, pray it specifically over the thing you fear, and answer the lie out loud with the truth. Do this every time the fear comes this week.

The fear will keep talking. Your job is only to make sure it does not get the last word.
